messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: prod: increased 5xx rate from 0.4% -> 7.2% over 2m for /v1/generate (canary pool). Paging on-call.
lee_ops: got the page, I'm on it. caret: checking canary pool and recent deploys.
sam_sre: I see repeated CrashLoopBackOffs on inference-worker-canary-*.pod in eu-west-1. kubectl shows OOMKilled then CrashLoopBackOff.
maria_eng: which deploy? deploy-bot just did a staggered canary for release 2026.03.15-3 at 19:07 UTC. I see a manifest change to livenessProbe and a new env flag ENABLE_FAST_BATCHING=true.
lee_ops: running quick checks: `kubectl -n prod get pods -l app=inference-worker -o wide` -> lots of restarts on canary nodes, non-canary replicas healthy.
sam_sre: HPA spike noted: target CPU spiked to 750% because failed pods kept restarting; HPA reacted and spawned more pods on nodes being drained earlier for a kernel patch rollout.
emily_prodsec: customer-impact: several mid-tier customers reporting increased latency and 502s during streaming. CS triage counting ~8 customers affected, potential SLA hits.
jordan_support: have started an incident template to notify customers A/B. Will advise on mitigation steps once we have root cause.
lee_ops: suspect combo: staggered node-drain + manifest change (liveness change + batching flag) -> pods killed mid-init, causing restarts and HPA cascade. Also nodes under memory pressure from previous batch jobs.
maria_eng: canary manifest diff:
```
- livenessProbe: httpGet: /healthz
  failureThreshold: 3
+ livenessProbe: httpGet: /healthz?fast=true
  failureThreshold: 1
+ env:
+  - name: ENABLE_FAST_BATCHING
+    value: "true"
```
maria_eng: the new probe is stricter; combined with faster batching it's possible cold-start memory use is higher and fails the probe.
lee_ops: immediate mitigation: can we flip the feature flag off for canary? which rollout strategy allows a kill-switch?
maria_eng: the flag is behind feature-flag service. I'll try to toggle for canary group only.
deploy-bot: feature-flag: toggled ENABLE_FAST_BATCHING -> false for target:canary (ok).
maria_eng: toggled. monitor logs.
sam_sre: logs still show CrashLoopBackOff for several pods. probe failures continue. maybe the probe endpoint expecting query param isn't present on old runtime, so probe 404 -> fails.
lee_ops: run quick patch: restore previous livenessProbe threshold via kubectl patch to canary deployment to prevent immediate restarts while we evaluate.
maria_eng: applying patch: `kubectl -n prod patch deployment inference-worker-canary --type='json' -p='[ {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/livenessProbe/failureThreshold","value":3} ]'`
lee_ops: patch applied.
sam_sre: restarting canary pods gracefully: `kubectl -n prod rollout restart deployment/inference-worker-canary`
maria_eng: rolling restarts started. watching logs: first pods come up with no liveness failures now, but memory still high on some nodes.
lee_ops: nodes where pods landed are under memory pressure; cordoning new scheduled nodes to avoid tight packing. Also scaling cluster up temporarily.
deploy-bot: autoscaler: adding 3 nodes to eu-west-1 compute-pool (requested).
emily_prodsec: customer impact update: error rate dropping from 7.2% -> 2.1% after flag toggle + patch. still above baseline. CS notified customers about degraded performance and mitigation steps.
jordan_support: sending standard incident notification to affected customers now.
maria_eng: we should still rollback the canary manifest entirely and re-run canary with smaller probe change. Recommend `kubectl rollout undo` for canary.
lee_ops: agree. initiating rollback: `kubectl -n prod rollout undo deployment/inference-worker-canary --to-revision=5` (revision 5 = previous stable)
sam_sre: undo applied; monitoring pods.
deploy-bot: deploy: rollout undo started by lee_ops for inference-worker-canary (rev -> 5).
lee_ops: after rollback, pod restarts reduced; HPA target scaled back down. Preparing handoff: I'll remain on-call for 30m then hand to sam_sre.
sam_sre: I'll take the 30m follow-up and watch for regressions.
emily_prodsec: request capture: list of affected customers + timestamps of errors for postmortem. Jordan, can you aggregate?
jordan_support: collecting logs and CS reports; will attach customer IDs and error windows to incident ticket.
lee_ops: root cause (preliminary): simultaneous staggered node drain + an overly strict liveness change + feature flag for faster batching increased cold-start memory leading to probe 404/fail loop. HPA reacted and amplified failures.
maria_eng: action items: 1) revert canary manifest in git (done via rollback) 2) change liveness probe to gentler thresholds + add readiness probe separate 3) add canary runbook step: pause node drains while canary is ramping 4) add test for probe param compatibility to CI
sam_sre: infra actions: 1) update node-drain playbook to pause on rolling canary 2) limit HPA max replicas for canary group 3) add memory headroom alert
emily_prodsec: communication: draft postmortem + customer impact blurb. we should be conservative on SLA exposure until ticket aggregation complete.
lee_ops: handoff: @sam_sre now on-call for this thread. I'll leave notes in the incident ticket. If error rate creeps above 3% revert full release and trigger emergency page.
sam_sre: acknowledged. I'll watch dashboards and logs, will escalate to infra if node pressure resurfaces.
deploy-bot: incident closed? no - ongoing monitoring. next update in 15m.
oncall-bot: INCIDENT: prod-canary-memory-probe-regression | Sev: P2 | Status: monitoring | Assignee: sam_sre | Thread: 2198765432"
